correctness.rationale: For dependent S one point is in the affine hull of the other points and cannot be separately excluded by an affine flat. For any affine-independent S of size ≤ k+1, extend to k+1 points and construct a k-flat for each nonempty trace using a linear functional 0 on positive difference vectors and 1 on excluded vectors; a disjoint parallel k-flat realizes the empty trace. Thus all and only independent sets through rank k+1 are shattered. Ordered affine-independent m-tuples are q^d times ∏_(i=0)^(m-2)(q^d−q^i); dividing by m! gives all coefficients, with m=0 equal1. An induction bounding positive branches of the linear k-subspace membership class by k proves affine Ldim≤k+1 and the shattered support provides ≥k+1. Quotienting the span of t positive independent points yields residual rank k+1−t. The proof handles k=0, q=2 and prime-power extensions; the 14-case checker corroborates but is not infinite evidence.

value.rationale: The claim is a full natural rank-and-field-uniform classification of a canonical finite-geometry incidence concept family, including every shattered point configuration, exact f-vector and the adaptive rank remaining after independent positive evidence. This is a motivated identification of learning-theoretic shattering with an affine-matroid truncation and a precise finite-field sampling invariant, not a made-up parameter slice or claim that the standard rank count alone is new. It distinguishes exact-k-flat concepts from more familiar at-most-k affine classes, and supplies a complete natural classification without needing a downstream theorem.
